title: Missing Values & Outliers
interviewAnswer: Missing values are generated by a process, not merely blank cells. I distinguish structural absence, measurement failure and unknown values, then reason about MCAR, MAR and MNAR assumptions relative to observed data. Dropping rows is defensible only when the target population and missingness mechanism make the resulting selection acceptable. Simple median or most-frequent imputation is a strong predictive baseline; indicators can preserve the fact that a value was missing; model-based or multiple imputation is useful when uncertainty in the missing values matters for inference. Every imputer is fitted inside training folds, and time-aware features use only historically available values. I compare native missing-value models with pipeline baselines, evaluate performance by missingness pattern and cohort, and monitor rates and upstream causes. Imputation does not recover truth: it supplies a modeling value under assumptions that must be versioned and stress-tested.
keyPoints: Separate structural absence, collection failure, censoring and semantically unknown categories before choosing a treatment.
MCAR, MAR and MNAR describe the missingness mechanism relative to variables and assumptions, not a property proven by a quick test.
Fit imputers and missingness-derived feature selection only on training folds.
Single imputation understates uncertainty for statistical inference; multiple imputation propagates between-imputation variation under its model.
Missingness rates and patterns are production data-quality signals even when the model accepts NaN natively.
why: A missing laboratory result may mean the test was not ordered, the instrument failed, the patient declined or the result arrived after prediction. Those mechanisms carry different information and risks. Dropping incomplete rows can change the population; filling zero can invent a real value; global imputation leaks validation distribution; and elaborate imputers can create false precision. Missingness may itself be predictive because policy determines what gets measured, but using that signal can fail when the policy changes. A strong treatment begins with semantics and lineage, establishes simple leakage-safe baselines, evaluates patterns rather than only global averages, and separates predictive convenience from causal or inferential claims.
intuition: If umbrellas are missing from a survey mostly on sunny days, absence is informative about weather. Replacing every blank with the mean may let a model work, but it does not make the umbrellas observed. The blank and the replacement answer different questions: one describes the collection process, the other gives the algorithm a numeric input.
deepDive: Missing-data handling joins data semantics, selection mechanisms, estimation uncertainty and production reliability. Predictive pipelines can use robust imputation and indicators, while inference may require explicit multiple-imputation or selection models. Valid evaluation recreates missingness at prediction time, keeps learned fills within folds and monitors policy-driven changes in measurement.
workedExample: Income is more often missing for precarious workers. Dropping incomplete rows produces a higher-income evaluation population and can overstate loan-model performance for the people most likely to have missing income.

imp=SimpleImputer(strategy='median',add_indicator=True).fit(Xtr)
sk_train=imp.transform(Xtr); sk_test=imp.transform(Xte)

commonMistakes.misconception: Mean imputation restores the missing values.
commonMistakes.correction: It supplies a constant modeling value, shrinks variance and does not recover individual truth.

commonMistakes.misconception: MAR can be proven from observed data.
commonMistakes.correction: Dependence on unobserved values is untestable without assumptions or external information; use domain reasoning and sensitivity analysis.

commonMistakes.misconception: Native NaN support removes all missing-data concerns.
commonMistakes.correction: Semantics, availability, selection, drift and upstream failures remain even if the estimator accepts NaN.

commonMistakes.misconception: Forward and backward filling are equivalent preprocessing.
commonMistakes.correction: Backward filling uses future observations and leaks in forward-looking prediction.

followUps.question: When is a missingness indicator useful?
followUps.answer: When absence carries predictive information not recoverable from the fill, with policy stability and subgroup implications evaluated.

followUps.question: Why fit median imputation inside CV?
followUps.answer: A global median lets validation values influence their own transformed representation and makes the evaluation pipeline unlike deployment.

followUps.question: When is multiple imputation preferable?
followUps.answer: When parameter or decision uncertainty from missing values matters and a defensible imputation model plus combination analysis is available.

production: Version field semantics, null tokens, availability cutoffs, structural states, fitted imputer values, indicator schema and fallback hierarchy. Fit all learned missing-data operations inside train folds and maintain online-offline parity. Test all-missing rows and columns, unseen categories, invalid sentinels and time direction. Report performance by missingness pattern with independent-unit uncertainty. Monitor missing and co-missing rates, feature freshness, imputed fraction and fallback use; alert on source-level changes, canary measurement-policy updates and route to a safe model or human review when critical coverage fails.
math: Let R_j=1 indicate feature X_j is observed. MCAR assumes R independent of observed and missing values; MAR assumes missingness is conditionally independent of missing values given observed variables; MNAR allows dependence on unobserved values even after conditioning. Mean imputation minimizes observed squared reconstruction error for a constant but shrinks variance and correlations. Multiple imputation combines estimate mean Qbar and within-imputation variance Ubar with between-imputation variance B; total variance is Ubar+(1+1/m)B under Rubin-style rules and compatible assumptions.

lab.goal: Implement training-only median imputation with indicators, verify pipeline parity, and prove validation extremes cannot change fitted values.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
Xtr=np.array([[1.,np.nan],[2.,10.],[100.,20.],[3.,np.nan]]); Xte=np.array([[np.nan,1.],[4.,np.nan]])
median=np.nanmedian(Xtr,axis=0); indicator_cols=np.isnan(Xtr).any(axis=0)
def transform(X,median,indicator_cols):
    X=np.asarray(X,float); indicator=np.isnan(X).astype(float)[:,indicator_cols]; filled=np.where(np.isnan(X),median,X); return np.c_[filled,indicator]
manual_train=transform(Xtr,median,indicator_cols); manual_test=transform(Xte,median,indicator_cols)
lab.useIt:
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
imp=SimpleImputer(strategy='median',add_indicator=True).fit(Xtr)
sk_train=imp.transform(Xtr); sk_test=imp.transform(Xte)
lab.verifyIt:
assert np.allclose(median,[2.5,15.])
assert np.allclose(manual_train,sk_train) and np.allclose(manual_test,sk_test)
assert np.allclose(imp.statistics_,median)
Xte_extreme=Xte.copy(); Xte_extreme[0,0]=1e9; assert np.allclose(imp.statistics_,median)
assert manual_test.shape==(2,3) and manual_test[0,2]==0 and manual_test[1,2]==1
assert indicator_cols.tolist()==[False,True]
lab.shipIt: Persist imputer statistics and indicator schema, test online null semantics and extreme missingness, and alert on source-specific coverage changes before silent degradation spreads.

description: Missing-value handling begins with the data-generating and collection process. This chapter distinguishes structural absence, unknown categories, sensor failure, censoring and delayed availability; defines MCAR, MAR and MNAR; and explains why these assumptions are rarely proven from observed data alone. It compares row or column deletion, constant, mean, median, mode, groupwise, nearest-neighbor, iterative and multiple imputation, missingness indicators and estimators with native missing-value support. It shows how single imputation changes variance and relationships, why target-aware imputation can leak, and how multiple imputation propagates uncertainty for inference. Worked examples expose selection bias from complete-case analysis and the predictive value of a measurement indicator. The lab implements training-only median imputation and indicators, verifies scikit-learn pipeline behavior and checks that validation extremes cannot alter fitted fills. Production guidance versions missing-value semantics and fallback rules, monitors rates and patterns by source and cohort, tests all-missing and new-category cases, and treats sudden missingness as an upstream incident rather than silently masking it.
learningObjectives: Classify missingness semantics and reason explicitly about MCAR, MAR and MNAR assumptions.
Choose deletion, imputation, indicators or native handling for predictive and inferential goals.
Build fold-local imputation pipelines and test leakage, edge cases and missingness patterns.
Monitor missing-data behavior as both a model input and a production data-quality signal.

deepSections.title: Identify why a value is absent
deepSections.body: Start with the field's meaning and collection workflow. Structural absence means the field does not apply, such as pregnancy-related data for an ineligible record; encode that state separately from an attempted but failed measurement. An unknown categorical value differs from a novel category and from an empty string introduced by parsing. Censoring means the value is only known above or below a limit and should preserve that bound. Delayed values may be available for training today but not at prediction time, making them temporal leakage rather than ordinary missingness. MCAR, MAR and MNAR are assumptions about the response indicator. MCAR is strong and uncommon; MAR can condition on rich observed covariates; MNAR requires sensitivity, selection or pattern-mixture reasoning. Observed data cannot generally distinguish MAR from MNAR without external assumptions. Document domain evidence and plausible departures rather than assigning a label mechanically.

deepSections.title: Simple treatments are useful when their estimand is clear
deepSections.body: Complete-case deletion changes the target population to rows with every required value. It is unbiased for some parameters under MCAR and particular models, but loses power and can be severely selected otherwise. Dropping a mostly missing feature may be sensible when it adds no reliable operational value, but future availability improvements can change that decision. Mean and median imputation provide deterministic, stable baselines; median is less sensitive to tails. Most-frequent or explicit unknown tokens support categories, provided structural states remain distinguishable. A constant outside the valid range plus a missing indicator often lets flexible models learn separate behavior. Groupwise fills use extra structure but require enough training support and a fallback hierarchy. Never use labels or future group statistics unless the construction is nested and available. Compare against native missing-value estimators rather than assuming imputation is always superior.

deepSections.title: Advanced imputation adds assumptions, not missing truth
deepSections.body: K-nearest-neighbor and iterative regression imputers use relationships among features and can preserve more structure when those relationships transport. They are computationally heavier, sensitive to scaling and model specification, and must be fitted per training fold. A single completed dataset treats estimated fills as known and tends to understate uncertainty for coefficients, intervals and downstream inference. Multiple imputation draws several plausible completed datasets under an imputation model, fits the analysis to each and combines estimates using within- and between-imputation variation. The imputation model should include variables related to missingness and analysis, respect bounds and types, and avoid using post-outcome data. Multiple imputation does not solve MNAR automatically; perform sensitivity analyses across plausible missingness models. For pure prediction, honest held-out performance may matter more than unbiased parameter interpretation, but uncertainty and subgroup harm still matter.

deepSections.title: Imputation belongs to the fold-specific procedure
deepSections.body: Split raw rows, groups and time before estimating medians, category frequencies, iterative relationships or indicators selected by frequency. A pipeline fits the imputer on each training fold and applies frozen values to validation. When target encoding or supervised feature selection follows imputation, the entire chain stays inside. Time-series forward filling must stop at the prediction cutoff and respect entity boundaries; backward filling is future leakage. Evaluate on naturally occurring missingness patterns and, when plausible, stress-test additional dropout by feature and cohort. Report performance for complete and incomplete rows, but recognize that these populations differ. Test all-missing columns, rows with every optional value missing, infinite values, unseen categories and transformed feature names. Compare prediction stability across reasonable imputation strategies rather than tuning many fills on the final test.

deepSections.title: Treat missingness as a monitored source behavior
deepSections.body: Version null tokens, parser rules, structural states, required fields, imputer statistics, indicator columns and fallback order with the model. Online and offline code must agree on whether empty strings, NaN, sentinel numbers and absent keys mean the same thing. Monitor missing rate, co-missing patterns, freshness and imputed fraction by source, feature, cohort and model version. A model may continue producing scores during an upstream outage, but that graceful degradation can conceal loss of information; define alert and fail-open or fail-closed thresholds. Log which fallbacks fired without exposing sensitive raw values. Revalidate after measurement policy changes because a missing indicator may encode clinician or reviewer behavior. Keep training-era distributions and canary predictions, and rollback or route to human review when critical feature coverage collapses.

workedExamples.title: Complete cases change the population
workedExamples.body: Income is more often missing for precarious workers. Dropping incomplete rows produces a higher-income evaluation population and can overstate loan-model performance for the people most likely to have missing income.

workedExamples.title: Indicator carries workflow information
workedExamples.body: A test is ordered mainly for high-risk patients. Median-imputing absent results plus an indicator allows the model to distinguish not-tested from an actual median result, but the signal may fail if ordering policy changes.

exercises.prompt: Why is filling a missing temperature with zero risky?
exercises.solution: Zero may be a valid and extreme temperature, conflating absence with measurement unless a justified sentinel and indicator are used.

exercises.prompt: What does multiple imputation add over one iterative fill?
exercises.solution: Several plausible datasets capture between-imputation variation so downstream uncertainty can reflect missing-value uncertainty under the model.

exercises.prompt: How should a time-series feature be filled for tomorrow's forecast?
exercises.solution: Use only values available by today's cutoff within the correct entity, with a declared maximum age and fallback; never backward-fill from tomorrow.
